correctness.rationale: Smooth plane quartics are canonical genus-three models, so their F2-rational automorphisms extend to PGL3(F2). At a rational projection center P, every projective fiber-fixing transformation is a shear I+P\otimes ell with ell(P)=0; precisely three nonidentity elations exist, giving possible group orders 1,2,4. The invariant-quartic expression shows a nontrivial fiberwise automorphism forces an inner center to be singular, hence all such centers are outer. Independent exhaustive binary homogeneous-quartic orbit enumeration covered all 32,767 nonzero masks, found 279 PGL3(F2) orbits, and exact geometric smoothness (three affine-chart Groebner unit-ideal tests) selected 78 smooth orbits comprising 10,920 forms. Checking all seven rational centers and their three elations independently reproduced class profiles (0,0):61, (1,0):14, (3,0):1, (2,1):1, (0,7):1 and weighted equation counts 9736/1134/28/21/1 respectively, hence 17 positive classes. A nontrivial full order-four deck group gives exactly the asserted Galois-point characterization.

originality.rationale: Nart–Ritzenthaler already give the full characteristic-two genus-three nonhyperelliptic curve classification and automorphism normal forms, so the 78 curve classes and the characteristic-two Klein Galois example are NOT new. Fukasawa–Miura–Takahashi define quasi-Galois points and prove general quartic bounds, with the Klein exceptional curve known. The candidate novelty is specifically the simultaneous distribution of fiber-fixing groups of orders two and four at every F2-rational center across all 78 arithmetic classes and weighted equations, which requires an elation-incidence refinement not explicitly stated in materially read main tables. Best-of-knowledge PASS qualified by possible implicit extraction from older stabilizer tables.
residual_risks: The extensive normal-model/stabilizer tables of Nart–Ritzenthaler may implicitly determine these exact center groups; an earlier table of rational elations would be decisive prior coverage.
Characteristic-two Galois-point special models and Klein extremal cases are known, so they must not be advertised as newly discovered.
Geometrically smooth (algebraic closure) rather than merely nonsingular at the seven rational points is essential to the census.

value.rationale: The seven rational points of PG(2,2) and partial deck groups are intrinsic arithmetic invariants of plane quartic projections. The completed joint distribution across every genus-three nonhyperelliptic F2 class distinguishes full Galois projections from merely quasi-Galois involutions, giving a natural complete arithmetic classification rather than a gratuitous table of coefficients. It is useful independently of the already known 78-class census.
